what_the_paper_would_let_us_do: Implement irbesartan from a source with first-order absorption. The only model read in full, Karatza and Karalis 2020 (PMID 32736091, in the archive; two compartments, apparent oral, 32 healthy men, no covariates), absorbs each dose through a delay differential equation, dA0/dt = -ka A0(t - T), with ka T = 0.511 > 1/e, so its input oscillates: 105% of the dose reaches plasma by 6.5 h and 5% flows back to the gut. No nonnegative input the engine can carry gets within 3.5% of that curve (a linear program over any number of pulses), and the best pulse discretisation built (12 default-form oral pulses, as hydrochlorothiazide's Weibull) misses it by 5.8% of the peak (6.4% at a 45 kg woman), ten times the 0.53% standard of docs/adding-a-drug.md, so irbesartan was withheld from PR #818. [decision] for Steven Shafer, raised 2026-11-19: accept Karatza with the 5.8% error stated, or wait for Hedaya and Helmy 2015 (PMID 25545238), whose model the Karatza paper borrowed for its blood-pressure simulations and which is expected to be first order (to be confirmed on the PDF). Karatza's model checked against the Avapro label (not fitted to it): CL/F 13.5 L/h inside the label's 11.8-17.6; Tmax 1.9 h inside 1.5-2 h; terminal half-life 8.2 h against 11-15 h. Karatza's text says nothing is absorbed for the first 1.68 h, but its Table 3 (Tmax 1-2 h at delays to 2.3 h) needs the dose held in the depot before time 0 (Monolix's history convention); that reading reproduces Table 3's Tmax exactly and AUC(0-48) within 0.8%. The Karatza draft (model, test, shared-file patch with the antihypertensive registry record and parameter rows) was not committed; its help-page narrative must be rewritten. Also needed whichever source is used: the drugDefaults row (Antihypertensives), a therapeuticRanges row (none_established), the pregnancy row (not_applicable, ARB fetotoxicity, as valsartan), the antihypertensive registry record and parameters, the three plasma-only rosters, and the Avapro label (archive copy NJ_dailymed-7885b2a8.pdf, md5 12123dca3f7ee8305bd81501a8cc7b64, card papers/digests/NJ_dailymed-7885b2a8.md) in papers/labels with its fdaLabels.csv row.

Liu M, Hu X, Liu J. The effect of hypothermia on isoflurane MAC in children. Anesthesiology 2001;94:429-432. The code says it was read, but its PDF is not in stanpumpRPapers (the archive check in docs/gas-engine-audit/PROMPT.md, section 9), so nobody can re-check the numbers against the source. File the PDF, write its card, and confirm each number below on the PDF. If one differs, change the constant and everything that pins or prints it, in a new pull request. The volatile agents' MAC rests on this paper's regression of isoflurane MAC on temperature in children (37, 34 and 31 C): MAC = 0.0784 T - 1.203. That gives GAS_MAC_ZERO_TEMPERATURE = 1.203/0.0784 = 15.3 C, or 4.6% of the normothermic MAC per degree. The R/physiology.R header says the paper's own text gives 'approximately 5.1%' and a zero at 16.2 C, neither of which follows from its regression. Check all three on the PDF. gasMacTemperatureFactor() applies the regression to sevoflurane, isoflurane and desflurane, to their MAC equivalents, and, since PR #858, to their thresholds (gasThresholdForTemperature()). A copy, PMID_11374601.pdf, is on Dr Shafer's Drive outside the archive, in the folders named CarlisleDownload.
